newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish PKO, Credit Suisse in fund deal.
newsitem.headline: Polish PKO, Credit Suisse in fund deal.

text.p: The state-owned PKO BP savings bank and Credit Suisse Group, which created a Trust Fund Corporation (TFP) in June, will sell the first units of their balanced fund on Wednesday, officials said on Tuesday.

PKO BP deputy president Andrzej Szeworski told a news conference that TFP planned to invest 60 percent of the balanced fund's assets in Polish equity and at least 30 percent in Polish debt instruments.
He did not say what the remaining 10 percent would be invested in.
"Up to 60 percent of investors' assets will be invested in shares. At least 30 percent...will be invested in Polish debt," Szeworski said.
TFP head Colin Horne, also present, said TFP would offer a higher rate of return on investment than the return on a one-year bank deposit, adding the fund targeted longer-term investors.
Horne said TFP planned to launch an equity fund and offer derivatives to investors by the end of the year.
The Trust Fund Corporation (TFP) was established by PKO BP and Credit Suisse in 1996 with a capital of 10 million zlotys.
